_comment: Synthetic course fixture for the chat_tutor offline evals (ADR 0023, issue #149). Plaintext by design: this data never touches the app database or its encryption boundary — FixtureRetrieval serves it straight to the agent. Concepts deliberately overlap the eval cases' topics so grounding evaluators have something to ground against.

documents.summary: Lecture notes covering limits as the foundation of derivatives, the definition of the derivative as a limit of difference quotients, and an introduction to the chain rule with worked examples.

concept_notes.name: Limits
concept_notes.description: The value a function approaches as the input approaches a point; the foundation of the derivative definition.

concept_notes.name: Derivatives
concept_notes.description: Instantaneous rate of change; the slope of the tangent line, defined as a limit of difference quotients.

concept_notes.name: Chain Rule
concept_notes.description: Differentiating composite functions: d/dx f(g(x)) = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).

documents.summary: Lab handout on writing recursive functions in Python: identifying the base case, the recursive step, and tracing the call stack for factorial and Fibonacci.

concept_notes.name: Recursion
concept_notes.description: A function that calls itself on a smaller subproblem until reaching a base case.

concept_notes.name: Base Case
concept_notes.description: The non-recursive branch that terminates the recursion; without it the call stack overflows.

concept_notes.name: Big-O Notation
concept_notes.description: Asymptotic upper bound on running time; naive Fibonacci recursion is O(2^n).

documents.summary: Course syllabus for IDS 201 Interdisciplinary Foundations: weekly topics spanning calculus, computing, biology, physics, and economics, with two midterms and a final project.

concept_notes.name: Photosynthesis
concept_notes.description: Conversion of light energy to chemical energy in chloroplasts; light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle.

concept_notes.name: Newton's First Law
concept_notes.description: An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net external force (inertia).

messages.content: Can we go over derivatives again? I got lost in lecture.
Of course! Before we dive in: in your own words, what does a derivative measure?
I think it's the slope of a function at a point?
Exactly — the slope of the tangent line. And we get it by taking a limit of difference quotients. What happens to (f(x+h)-f(x))/h as h shrinks?
It approaches the instantaneous rate of change.
Well put. Next time let's connect this to the chain rule, which is where you said things got fuzzy.
